The connection chip is the part that had to be legible: a page frozen at
    the last thing somebody's card said and a person who never changes
    anything are indistinguishable otherwise, so the ended state says so in
    a sentence and not only in a tag. The band grows with its contents now,
    since a fixed 200px clipped a face off the top edge once a photo and a
    chip stood above the name.
    
    The two apps also disagreed about words. "Private context" is a name
    nothing else in Haven ever used; iOS calls the same field "What you
    remember" and says how it is read, so the web says both. Only the label
    and the supporting line change -- the field, its id and what it saves are
    untouched.
    
    The reach rows lead with the platform somebody chose, which is what
    choosing it meant, folded through samePlatform because the server stores
    that string verbatim and a raw === would bury the row they picked.
    
    Pinned to the iOS source the way reach.test.ts pins the addresses:
    PersonScreen.swift and PersonModel.swift are read off disk and the
    sentences, labels and separators parsed out of them, each pin asserting
    its parse found something before asserting anything about the web.
    Nothing imports across the platform boundary, so a sentence reworded on
    the phone drifts here in silence.
